title: Decoder-only LLM
description: Autoregressive decoder-only language model architecture scaling to billions of parameters.
name: Decoder-only LLM
summary: Decoder-only Large Language Models construct autoregressive representations by masking future tokens. They are designed to model joint probabilities of text sequences, enabling few-shot reasoning at massive parameter scales.
use_when: Implementing general-purpose language reasoning, text completion, or instruction-following interfaces.
avoid_when: Strict feature embedding extraction is needed, where bi-directional encoders perform better.
pros: State-of-the-art zero-shot and few-shot reasoning capabilities.
Unified text-in, text-out interface simplifies application architectures.
Can follow complex formatting and schema instructions dynamically.
cons: Extremely high compute and memory requirements for serving and training.
Inference speed is bounded by token-by-token sequence generation.

key_hyperparams.name: max_seq_len
key_hyperparams.note: Maximum context length. Bounded by positional embedding capacity.

quick_start:
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM
import torch

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf')
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained('meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf', torch_dtype=torch.float16)
inputs = tok("Once upon a time", return_tensors="pt")
out = model.generate(**inputs, max_length=20)
